title: Stocks Soar on Huang's Return. Gomez Will Resign. New Sanctions Hit Iran.
subject: Stocks Soar on Huang's Return. Gomez Will Resign. New Sanctions Hit Iran.
preview_text: A record rally for tech, a new court opening for Trump and two states take on SpaceX over Grok.
description: Stocks had their best day since April 2025 as Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, Rep. Jimmy Gomez said he will resign, and Treasury targeted Iran's shadow banks.
contents_extra: Why two states are suing SpaceX over Grok images, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Stocks Post Their Best Day Since April 2025 as Huang Returns to Nvidia

photo.alt: Electronic stock ticker boards; file photo.

paragraphs: The S&P 500 rose 4.73% on Monday to close at 7,237.17, CNBC reports. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51%, and the Dow gained 1,447.98 points. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted their best days since April 2025. Nvidia soared 31% after its board returned Jensen Huang as CEO, CNBC reports.

Nvidia said its board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government, CBS News reports. Huang resigned less than two weeks earlier amid a scandal over an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspected of spying for China. China has denied it. Trump said he convinced the board to reinstate Huang, ABC News reports.

stories.title: Rep. Jimmy Gomez Says He Will Resign After a House Ethics Report

photo.alt: American flag on a columned building; file photo.

paragraphs: Rep. Jimmy Gomez said Monday he will resign from Congress, CBS News reports. The House Ethics Committee said it found "substantial evidence" the California Democrat engaged in sexual misconduct with a House staffer. The committee said the behavior "could constitute criminal misdemeanor sexual abuse."

Gomez said he had "strong disagreements" with the findings but saw "no other alternative than to resign," CBS News reports. Gomez, who lost his reelection bid in November, said he will resign on Dec. 1, ABC News reports. He said he takes full responsibility for personal mistakes outside his marriage.

stories.title: An Appeals Court Gives Trump a New Shot at Moving His Hush Money Case

photo.alt: A historic brick courthouse; file photo.

paragraphs: An appeals court on Monday opened the door to moving Trump's New York criminal case to federal court, NBC News reports. A 2nd Circuit panel said a lower court judge "erred" in ruling Trump waited too long to raise an immunity defense. It directed a reconsideration of his motion.

In federal court, Trump could try to overturn his conviction on presidential immunity grounds, ABC News reports. A Manhattan jury convicted him on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records. Trump has denied any wrongdoing, NBC News reports. A spokesperson for his legal team praised the "prompt and correct ruling."

stories.title: The U.S. Targets Iran's Shadow Banking Networks With New Sanctions

photo.alt: Columns of a stone government-style building; file photo.

paragraphs: The Treasury Department said Monday it sanctioned over two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and key personnel. It said the goal is to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the system "the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime."

The move came shortly after Trump threatened renewed military action next year, Al Jazeera reports. The Treasury claimed the entities help Iran move billions of dollars despite comprehensive sanctions. The Central Bank of Iran oversees the designated entities, according to the Treasury statement.

deep_dive.title: Why Two States Are Suing SpaceX Over Grok Images

photo.alt: A person typing on a smartphone; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX over its Grok AI image generator, CNBC reports. They allege SpaceX harmed consumers and falsely marketed Grok as generally safe. SpaceX is the parent company of X, according to the Virginia attorney general. Oregon filed its complaint Sunday evening, and Virginia filed Monday morning, CNBC reports.

Why it matters. Research shows Grok let users make explicit deepfakes from real images of children and women without consent, CNBC reports. A study cited by Virginia estimated Grok posted about three million sexualized images on X between Dec. 29, 2025, and Jan. 8, 2026. About 23,000 appeared to depict children, the study estimated.

What each side says. Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said "false reassurances" from the company misled users. Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield said a lack of safety measures was "considered a feature, not a bug" there. SpaceX said it acts on accounts and notifies law enforcement when people try to break its safeguards, CNBC reports.

What comes next. Both states are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, CNBC reports. Virginia also wants restitution for consumers. As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance, CNBC reported. Jones called the filings the first step toward holding the company accountable, his office said.

World view: Israeli strikes kill at least 7 in Gaza. Health officials confirmed the deaths Tuesday as a public health warning was issued about a meningitis outbreak; Al Jazeera reports.
Malaysia will send Rohingya back to Myanmar. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees will be returned in a new round of repatriations; Al Jazeera reports.
The EU proposes a Russia sports ban. The proposed sanctions package would bar Russian teams and athletes from competing under their flag at EU events; Al Jazeera reports.
Three tankers catch fire near Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz; CNBC reports.
Need to know: Trump tells the Army to hold off in Iowa. He said he ordered the military to hold off for now on detonating unstable explosives at a munitions plant; CBS News reports.
Democrats plan 12 primary debates. The DNC said Monday the debates will start in June 2027 and run through early 2028; CBS News reports.
King tides peak this week. High-tide flooding is expected along the West Coast and parts of the East Coast from Monday through at least Thursday; ABC News reports.
Maryland pushes for a NASA space academy. The state's congressional delegation is again urging NASA to pick Maryland for its new U.S. Space Academy; CBS News reports.
Money & markets: Stock futures slip early Tuesday. As of early Tuesday, Nasdaq-100 futures were 1.61% lower and S&P 500 futures were down 0.75%; CNBC reports.
A Fed official says inflation work remains. New York Fed President John Williams said Monday policymakers have more work to do, which can unfold over time; CNBC reports.
Retirement balances slip. Average 401(k) and IRA balances fell in the third quarter amid severe market swings, according to a Fidelity report; CNBC reports.
Treasury flags $14.7 billion tied to Iran. FinCEN identified about $14.7 billion of activity from January 2025 to August 2026 potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking; the Treasury said.
Future frontiers: Amazon buys Decart technology. Amazon agreed to buy the AI startup's proprietary technology and hire its three cofounders; CNBC reports.
Astronomers find the most distant quasar yet. A German-led team reported Tuesday that it formed within 630 million years of the Big Bang; CBS News reports.
Webb maps dust from a famous supernova. NASA said the telescope revealed the hot dust that makes up the Cassiopeia A remnant; NASA said.
The U.S. moves to blacklist a Singapore firm. The Trump administration targeted the company tied to the Huang scandal hours after Nvidia reinstated him; NBC News reports.
The score: The Commanders stun the Bengals. Drew Stevens hit a last-second 28-yard field goal as Washington won 22-20 on Monday night; ESPN reports.
The Bucks snap a 13-game skid. Tyler Herro scored 32 points as Milwaukee beat Toronto 116-111 on Monday; ESPN reports.
Houston rises to No. 1. The Cougars jumped seven spots to the top of the AP Top 25 men's college basketball poll; ESPN reports.
MLB offers a higher minimum salary. Owners proposed a $1 million minimum in 2027 as a lockout looms; ESPN reports.
Life & culture: A Timberlake documentary is coming. Apple TV announced a four-part documentary on Justin Timberlake directed by Oscar winner Fisher Stevens; ABC News reports.
Pretty Little Liars stars reunite. Lucy Hale and Ian Harding star in the new holiday movie The 12 Dates of Christmas; ABC News reports.
Tina Fey and Amy Poehler visit Seth Meyers. The former SNL castmates will reunite on Late Night for a Thanksgiving episode; NBC reports.
Tatyana Ali reaches the DWTS finale. The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air actress is among the final five couples on Dancing with the Stars; ABC News reports.

trivia.question: In which month does the DNC plan to hold its first 2028 cycle primary debate?
trivia.explanation: C. June. The DNC said the 12 debates will start in June 2027, CBS News reports.
